Describe the concrete problem and resulting behavior. Name the applicable requirement IDs, company capability and targeted surface/data revision.

## Change and scope

- What changes for the user or operator?
- Which source, method, permission or release boundaries are affected?
- What exact code/data/config versions were checked?

## Validation

Record relevant checks and their results, including skipped or unavailable dependencies. For UI work, include actual behavior and desktop/tablet/phone evidence. Technical checks do not supply domain or consumer acceptance.

## Evidence and remaining work

Link the source/review receipts and explicit remaining gaps. Keep reported facts, verified findings, accepted uses and actual execution separate. For evidence revisions, include exact before/after accounting and preserved lineage.

## Publication and operations

Confirm that selected files and outgoing history were reviewed for credentials, personal data, source-use rights and asset licenses. Describe any migration, rollback, privacy, budget or operating impact. Public GitHub must not receive guest stores, transcripts, local credentials, database dumps or unreviewed bulk evidence.
